meta.title: CMU CS Academy — CS1

locator_titles.7: New Shapes, Local Variables, For Loops

meta.caveat: Mapped from the teacher's own unit-by-unit scope-and-sequence analysis (porttack.com, "CodeHS vs CMU", Appendix C), not from CMU's official standards document -- that document omits AP.14, which this mapping argues (with evidence from the Creative Task's own design step) is actually taught.

9-12.AP.12.note: Math/random/nested loops (unit 8) and 2D lists/board-game logic (unit 11) both involve choosing and adapting existing algorithms.

9-12.AP.13.note: Lists and 2D lists are core, assessed content (units 10-11), not an optional add-on.

9-12.AP.14.note: Woven through every conditionals/loop unit (3-5, 7-9) and made explicit in the Creative Task's own design step, which has students list the concepts they plan to use and justify why -- the standard's own language, 'justify the selection.' Not in CMU's own official standards document; the teacher's own classroom analysis argues it should be.

9-12.AP.15.note: Iterative development through events (mouse, key, step) recurs across units 2-6 and the final project (unit 12).

9-12.AP.16.note: Helper functions, introduced in unit 3, are decomposition into subproblems.

9-12.AP.17.note: Modular design via functions, methods, and library calls across units 2, 4, 7, and 10.

9-12.AP.18.note: Design-for-audience is the Creative Task's rubric, but the rubric itself does not require a feedback step -- CMU claims the standard on the task's design intent; whether it's actually met depends on the teacher building a feedback step in. In this teacher's own classroom it is.

9-12.AP.19.note: Not taught in CS1 -- software license limitations are deliberately deferred to AP CS Principles, where this teacher covers it directly with his own materials.

9-12.AP.20.note: The Creative Task's build-reflect-revise cycle runs ten times a year.

9-12.AP.21.note: Real-time shared-editor pair programming is built into every unit, not a capstone.

9-12.AP.22.note: The Creative Task requires describing the program and reflecting on what changed and why -- documentation of design decisions, ten times a year.
